invariant: INV-31b — Raw DB import is distinguished from UNSAFE raw DB import. Every sensitive-domain route that touches the database directly must carry an explicit classification. Unclassified sensitive direct DB usage and forbidden-direct-db usage fail the contract test; all other classifications are tolerated (some are migration-tracked).

allowed-system-route.description: System/infrastructure route with no tenant-scoped data exposure (health, readiness, schema introspection, maintenance). Direct DB access is acceptable.

allowed-admin-route.description: Platform/admin-gated management or diagnostic route. Access is restricted to elevated operators; direct DB access is acceptable under that gate.

requires-org-scope-wrapper.description: Tenant-bound route whose safe pattern is an org-scope / ownership wrapper (e.g. enforcePilotOwnership, grievance org-access, getOrgScopedDb). Tolerated. Entries flagged migration:true are acknowledged gaps queued for a later DB-hardening wave.

requires-rls-context.description: Tenant-bound route whose safe pattern is withRLSContext / withSystemContext session scoping. Tolerated. Entries flagged migration:true are acknowledged gaps queued for a later DB-hardening wave.

legacy-deprecated.description: Known legacy route slated for removal/replacement. Tolerated but tracked for sunset; do not extend.

forbidden-direct-db.description: Direct DB access that is not permitted and must be removed or wrapped. FAILS the contract test.

unclassifiedPolicy.description: Any sensitive-domain route with direct DB access that is not present in `classifications` is treated as unclassified-sensitive and FAILS. This is the fail-closed governance pressure: adding raw DB to a sensitive domain forces an explicit classification.
